messages:
jess_support: Hey team — ACME prod saw a big burst this morning and their dedicated pool didn't ramp quickly enough. Customers hit 429/504s and requests queued for ~90s. Can someone triage? :eyes:
acme_prod_ops: Repro steps I ran: synthetic burst ~5k rps for 2m. First 25s ok, then errors spiked. I grabbed events and kube logs, attaching excerpts below.
ryan_eng: Can you paste the attach / kube-scheduler events? curious if this is imagepull, node pressure, or autoscaler pacing.
acme_prod_ops: sure, snippets:```Events: 
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s (x12 over 90s)  default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient memory, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
PodStatus: OOMKilled x3
Container: attach error: rpc attach failed: handshake timeout after 30s
```
mina_sre: I pulled control-plane logs — we saw a burst of OOM evictions, then the cluster-autoscaler requested scale up but many new nodes were preemptible and reclaimed shortly after. That caused pod backfill to get stuck and attach handshakes to retry. Also saw 429s from our registry client when rotating tokens.
cory_infra: Confirmed. Registry auth rotation at 08:43 caused transient 403/429 for imagepulls. Couple that with OOM churn and scheduler backoff and the autoscaler couldn't get pods scheduled fast enough.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale_up requested from 12 -> 28 nodes (reason: cpu/memory pressure) at 4319991005
ryan_eng: So multi-factor: (1) OOM storm reduced capacity, (2) imagepull/auth rotation rate-limited registry, (3) new nodes preempted before pods fully started -> handshake retries. That explains the ~90s tail.
acme_prod_ops: Repro script I used (quick):```bash
# spawn mem-hungry pods to force evictions
for i in {1..50}; do kubectl run oom-$i --image=alpine --restart=Never -- /bin/sh -c 'dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/null bs=1M count=1M; sleep 300' & done
# then blast traffic with hey
hey -n 100000 -c 500 https://acme.example/api/generate
```
mina_sre: Quick mitigations: 1) increase dedicated pool min_replicas for this customer by +4, 2) enable a short warm-standby (pre-warmed nodes) for burst windows, 3) add jitter/retry improvements to registry client during token rotation, 4) mark some nodes non-preemptible for critical customers.
ryan_eng: Long term: tune autoscaler backoff to avoid aggressive backfill that depends on ephemeral nodes, add faster handshake path (skip heavy init for warm-standby), and surface attach handshake latency metric to console.
cory_infra: I've raised a patch to registry client to limit concurrent token refreshes per cluster and exponential-backoff 403 -> push tomorrow.
jess_support: Action items for CS: propose min_replicas bump + warm-standby offer to ACME, ask infra to roll the registry patch, engineering to track attach-handshake metric. I'll loop in account. Thanks all :thumbsup:
mina_sre: Also note we should run a chaos test that combines token rotation + memory pressure to catch this earlier.
jess_support: Adding to runbook and scheduling a postmortem with ACME ops. Will update thread when done.
